category_title: Students with blindness and autism sensitive to environmental noise and tactile distractors
minimal_context: The student is in a regular inclusive classroom listening to the teacher's instructions on what materials to take out for an assignment.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Alright everyone, let's get started on the new assignment. Look up here at the front to see what materials you need to take out.

STUDENT: I don’t know where to start. The teacher needs to tell me exactly what to take out and what to do.

TUTOR: Just look here at the example I'm holding up, it shows everything you need.

STUDENT: They tell everyone to ‘look here’ and ‘look there’… but I can’t look so I don’t understand what they mean.

TUTOR: We need to keep moving, just try your best to get your things ready.

STUDENT: It’s bad when they say that! Things are going too fast and I still don't know what to take out or what to do.

options.A: Integrate music into theoretical learning, use it as a reward, or facilitate peer interaction through musical activities.
options.B: Revise the Behavioral Intervention Plan to include specific strategies for preventing escape attempts during the activity.
options.C: Implement relatively tight timelines for the student to complete the assignment and get their materials ready.
options.D: Place an exclusive display board in the classroom only for the student to display their assignments.
